structured_stats.description:
'''PVP''' is a gamemode where opponents must defend each other until one team wins. The enemies in '''PVP''' are based on various modes based on player rank, though instead of the goal of surviving to the final wave, players are meant to defeat their opponent by sending enemies at them. If the final wave is beaten, it will repeat indefinitely until one team loses. The health of enemies will also get boosted over time.

This mode can be played in Casual, which has no added restrictions, and in Ranked, where players from a team could ban up to two towers. In 1v1, each player can ban up to two towers each, which is reduced to one each in 2v2. This mode has three rank based difficulties:
#Basic Arena, based around [[Casual Mode|Casual]] mode, where players range from Private I to Private III.
#Molten Arena, based on [[Intermediate Mode|Intermediate]] and [[Molten Mode|Molten]] modes, where players range from Sergeant I to Lieutenant III.
#Fallen Arena, based on [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode, where players range from Major I to above rank.

If players span multiple difficulties (such as a Private I teaming with a Major I), then the highest ELO score amongst all players is used to determine the difficulty. In Casual, the arena is voted for at the beginning of the match.

Each difficulty ends with the [[Champion Templar]] as the final boss. A player's rank goes up and down with triumphs and loses in Ranked matches, giving them rewards through the [[PVP Season 0]].

'''PVP''' applies multiple restrictions to players. The most noticeable change is the player's loadout being reduced to four towers. Additionally, all exclusive categories and golden perks are prohibited. Another large change is consumables, as this mode has its own exclusive ones. Toggleable modifiers are also completely disabled here. To compensate, various towers receive statistical changes to either make them stronger, such as starter towers becoming far more viable or small adjustments to make towers perform against enemy hordes.

Every 8 seconds, players receive cash from an economy bonus. The economy bonus can be seen under the tower placement limit. It may be increased by sending enemies to the opponent, though not all enemies sent grant an economy boost. Additionally, {{Money|20}} is added to the bonus after each wave.

In 2v2 matches, a 20% health scale effect is applied, boosting the health of enemies. This is not present in 1v1.

Cash is only gained if an enemy is killed or, in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gained is a set amount of cash, which is not always equal to the enemy's health. It uses a slightly different method of distributing cash between players, as enemies split their cash between players, regardless of how much damage the player dealt to it. If, in a duo, one player does all the damage to an enemy, both players will receive 50% of the cash the enemy would normally give in solo. This means that in solo, you receive 100% of the cash when an enemy is killed, or it is damaged enough. With each additional player, this is reduced to 50% in duo, 33% in trio and 25% in quad. If it is a decimal, it gets rounded up or down depending on the decimal value. If it is at least 0.5, it gets rounded up. If it is less than 0.5, it gets rounded down. For example, the [[Hidden Boss]] gives {{Money|600}} when killed in 1v1 and {{Money|300}} in 2v2.

Leaving '''PVP''' in the middle of the match applies a penalty to the player which prevents them from playing '''PVP''' for a specified duration. This duration increases depending on the amount of prior penalties you have received. In Ranked matches, there is an additional penalty of ELO loss. These penalties can be avoided if the player rejoins the match.

==Description==
The '''PVP Season 0''' was the first PVP Season to be released in Tower Defense Simulator.

It was released on the 23rd of July 2025 and ended on the 22nd of October 2025.

==Season==
[[File:PVPSeason0.png|center|450px]]
'''PVP Season 0''' initially required 4 ranked matches to get ranked. Afterwards, players would gain [[file:ELO.png|24px|link=]]ELO which advances them through the season. [[file:ELO.png|24px|link=]]ELO was gained by winning matches and lost by losing matches. Playing against players with higher ranks would grant higher [[file:ELO.png|24px|link=]]ELO rewards than if the player was to play with others of the same or lower rank.

The player's rank was determined by their [[file:ELO.png|24px|link=]]ELO. If it was in a specific range, they would be moved to that rank. This could both boost them upwards, for example from Sergeant II to III, but also downwards, like from General III to General II.

18.75% (Quad) |rewards = {{Exp|0}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== '''PVP Test''' was a recurring test mode prior to the release of the [[PVP]] mode. The enemies in '''PVP Test''' were based on various modes based on player rank, though instead of the goal of surviving to the final wave, players were meant to defeat their opponent by sending enemies at them. If the final wave was beaten, it would repeat indefinitely until one team loses. Wins did not count as triumphs (except for [[Quests]]), but losing this mode counted as a loss. This mode could be played in Casual, which had no added restrictions, and in Ranked, where players from a team could ban up to two towers. This mode had three rank based difficulties. The first one is Low Rank, which was based around [[Casual Mode|Casual]] mode, the second was Mid Rank, which was based on [[Intermediate Mode|Intermediate]] and [[Molten Mode|Molten]] modes and the third was High Rank, that was based on [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode. Which one was started is based on the the player's rank. The player's rank goes up and down with triumphs and loses in Ranked matches. '''PVP Test''' applied multiple restrictions to players. The most noticeable change was the player loadout being reduced to four players. Additionally, all exclusive categories and golden perks were prohibited. Another large change was consumables, as this mode only allowed '''PVP Test''' exclusive ones. Every 8 seconds, players received cash from an economy bonus. The economy bonus could be seen under the tower placement limit. It could be increased by sending enemies to the opponent. Each send increased it by its own value and {{Money|20}} was added to the bonus after each wave. Cash was only obtained if an enemy was killed, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gotten was a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. In solo, the player received 100% of the cash when an enemy was killed or damaged enough. With each additional player, this decreased by 25%, which meant that in a quad, any specific player would only get up to 25% of the cash. This amount was distributed between players based on how much damage they dealt. However, if a player did not deal any damage, they would receive a percentage of the enemy's full cash upon its death or when it was damaged enough, which is 12.5% in duo, 16.7% in trio and 18.75% in quad. If it was a decimal, it got rounded up or down depending on the decimal value. If it was at least 0.5, it got rounded up. If it was less than 0.5, it got rounded down. For example, the [[Hidden Boss]] gave {{Money|600}} when killed in solo, {{Money|450}} in duo, {{Money|300}} in trio and {{Money|150}} in quad between the players that damaged it. Players that did not damage it received {{Money|75}} in duo, {{Money|100}} in trio and {{Money|113}} in quad. ==Rewards== '''PVP Test''' did not grant any rewards or badges upon completion. Some inherited from spawner enemy }} ==Description== The '''Corpse''' is an enemy that only appears when spawned through the [[Corpse (Attribute)|Corpse]] attribute. Uniquely, its statistics are actually heavily based on the enemy that summoned it, instead of having its own statistics, though it does have some statistics that do not change. This is because the '''Corpse''' is not its own enemy, it is actually the enemy it spawned from with a changed display name and altered statistics. Most notably, it has 100% defense, and it has the [[Corpse (Attribute)|Corpse]], [[Stun Immunity]] and [[Burn Immunity]] attributes. Its health is 75% of the enemy that it spawned from. Additionally, some of the attributes the enemy it spawned from are also inherited. The only exception to this is [[Hidden (Attribute)|Hidden]], which is removed upon the enemy's death. ==Appearance== The '''Corpse''' does not have a consistent appearance, as the model it uses is based on the enemy it spawned from, though it does have certain characteristics which are consistent between them all. The '''Corpse''' is the body of the enemy it spawned from made entirely out of black molten rocks. Any images present on the enemy, such as faces, will remain on them even as a '''Corpse'''. ==Strategy== *The '''Corpse''' is not a threatening enemy, as it cannot move to the entrance, meaning losing to it is impossible. Its main purpose is to act as a shield for enemies behind it. **However, it can be relatively an inconvenience with its 100% defense and tendency to distract towers from attacking actual enemies. **Towers like the [[Electroshocker]] or [[Toxic Gunner]] can be used to drop its defense, as it is very high. The [[Pyromancer]] cannot be used since it has [[Burn Immunity]]. **Towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Mortar]] can be used to take care of any corpses that are too far away from your main defenses with their high range. *The '''Corpse''' is required to be killed before a match can end. **Waves can be skipped while only '''Corpses''' are on the path, as that still grants the wave clear bonus. Additionally, infinite waves cannot be skipped at all. ***If you have the [[DJ Booth]], you can exploit this by repeatedly using its ''Drop The Beat'' ability on Green track to make as much cash as you want. *As the '''Corpse''' is technically not a unique, summoned enemy, but instead the slightly altered version of the enemy it spawned from, the [[Cowboy]] is able to generate cash from it. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Previous Variants}} MoltenCorpseMolten.png|First version (11 December 2024 – 12 March 2025) {{GalleryHeade

Prior to that date, there were no other rewards for triumphing '''Hidden Wave'''. |music-1 = [[File:Tower Defense Simulator OST - Hidden Wave Intro|thumb|center|250px]] |music-2 = [[File:(Official) Tower Defense Simulator OST - Hidden Wave|thumb|center|250px]] }} {{QuoteContainer| {{QuoteBox|GREETINGS PLAYER.
YOU HAVE PROVED YOURSELF QUITE SKILLFUL SO FAR...
BUT HOW SKILLFUL DO YOU THINK YOU ACTUALLY ARE?|Activating the Hidden Wave}} {{QuoteBox|LET'S PUT IT TO THE TEST
HIDDEN WAVE|Right before the Hidden Wave}} {{QuoteBox|ARE YOU READY?
SEE IF YOU CAN BEAT THIS!|Beginning of the Hidden Wave}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The legacy version of the '''Hidden Wave''' was a secret wave that could have been accessed by defeating wave 40 on [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode in 1,009 seconds (16 minutes and 49 seconds) or less. This wave was extremely difficult and spawned unique and powerful enemies. {{Coins|Coins}} and {{Exp|}} earned remained the same for [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode regardless if the '''Hidden Wave''' was triggered, but losing on the '''Hidden Wave''' only rewarded you with the rewards when losing on wave 40 [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode. Triumphing the '''Hidden Wave''' awarded a special {{RLinkB|2124477833|badge}}. Originally, there was no other reward, though after the 9th of June 2023 anyone with the badge is able to claim the [[Glitchy Nametag]] through the [[Gift Box]]. Accessing the wave was quite difficult as you needed to speedrun through [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode. This meant that you needed three or more other players to trigger the '''Hidden Wave'''. The '''Hidden Wave''' could not have been triggered on [[MEGA Servers]] through the time requirement (interestingly, the '''Hidden Wave''' could have been triggered on a [[MEGA Servers|MEGA Server]] if the player count was 4 or lower before wave 40 on [[Fallen Mode|Fallen]] mode). Certain maps were favored over others due to cliff space, space near the path entrance, etc. After the [[Overhaul v1.0|Overhaul Update]], the wave intro broke. You could still activate it, but the text box did not appear and the game did not acknowledge that the '''Hidden Wave''' had been activated. Additionally, the lighting filter did not change to a red hue with text glitching. The wave would change to 1, while the timer would change to 111111111111111120:00. The only way to know if you have triggered the '''Hidden Wave''' was if the triumph screen did not show after the final wave countdown after you defeated the [[Fallen King (Legacy)|Fallen King]]. The '''Hidden Wave''' has since been replaced with a [[Hidden Wave|modern version]]. ==Rewards== {| class="empty-table pad-5 align-center" style="width:90%; margin:0 auto" |[[File:GlitchyTag.gif|200px|link=Glitchy Nametag]] |- |[[Glitchy Nametag]] |} ==Enemies== {| class="empty-table pad-5 align-center" style="width:90%; margin:0 auto" |[[File:GlitchedGiant-0.png|125px|link=Glitched Giant]] |[[File:Bruh-0.png|125px|link=Bruh]] |[[File:Bug-0.png|125px|link=Bug]] |[[File:FrostHero2020.png|125px|link=Frost Hero (Frost Invasion)]] |[[File:Jaxe.png|125px|link=Jaxe (Nightmare Carnival)]] |[[File:MechanicalRot-0.png|125px|link=Mechanical Rot (Legacy)]] |- |[[Glitched Giant]]
